name: stylus-nexus
description: Stylus Nexus plugins for Claude Code + Codex.

plugins.name: release-ops
plugins.description: Five skills for getting a release out the door. npm-publish runs the full path -- preflight checks, semver bump, changelog entry, git push, publish -- and rotates an expired npm token through the browser instead of stopping to ask for a one-time code. version-check reads the commits since the last tag and recommends the bump. pr-wait blocks on CI checks and optionally merges when they pass. dependency-upgrade treats bulk bumps as a gated pipeline rather than a single update command, running type checks, tests, and E2E between batches. the-waiting estimates how long running CI jobs have left from their own history and spots runs stuck behind a cancelled run that never stopped.

plugins.name: second-opinion
plugins.description: Five skills built on one premise: a single model's confident answer is not evidence. llm-council runs a question through five advisors who analyse independently before synthesis; plan-arbiter compares, judges, and merges competing plans rather than picking one on vibes; spec-review checks a spec's claims against the real codebase before code is written, catching wrong data-model assumptions early; agent-watchdog audits another agent's work from its session or transcript; and debug-feedback-loop builds a deterministic pass/fail signal for a bug BEFORE hypothesising about causes.

plugins.name: hardening
plugins.description: Six pre-launch gates covering the unglamorous failures that reach production. rate-limit-audit inventories every endpoint calling a paid API and every auth endpoint, then checks each actually has a limit; exposure-scan checks installed packages across npm, Go, PyPI, RubyGems and MCP servers against threat-intelligence catalogs for known-compromised releases; auth-hardening is a session, cookie, CSRF and OAuth-scope audit; webhook-reliability covers signature verification, idempotency, retry and dead letters in both directions; privacy-audit inventories exactly what user data is collected and where it lands, checked against the code rather than the policy; and readiness-review is a read-only launch-readiness report covering code health, live database structure, and a look-only walk of the product as a non-admin test user, ending in a findings list the human files.

plugins.name: reporting-comms
plugins.description: Seven skills for turning agent output into something a person actually wants to read, and getting their judgment back. html renders plans, reviews, research, and comparisons as a single self-contained HTML artifact; visual-plan and visual-recap turn text plans and git diffs into interactive documents with diagrams, file maps, and annotated code; recap-table produces before/after and what-changed tables on demand; writing-clearly-and-concisely and human-writing tighten the prose itself, stripping AI tells, corporate register, and padding; and redline runs the other direction, handing a draft back to the human to edit and comment on in a browser and returning one Markdown review the agent applies.

plugins.name: codebase-intel
plugins.description: Four skills for building an accurate picture of a codebase and the libraries it depends on, before committing to a change. codebase-health surfaces complexity hotspots, churn, and bus factor when onboarding or planning a refactor; codebase-architecture-scanner generates layered architecture documentation with C4 and sequence diagrams; grill-with-docs challenges a plan against the existing domain model and sharpens terminology; and read-the-damn-docs stops guesses about third-party API behavior by going to the current documentation first.

plugins.name: ship-pipeline
plugins.description: Nine repo-agnostic skills for the ship half of the development loop. start-issue (full-issue intake including comments, prior-art check, baseline capture, branch naming), db-truth (ground schema claims in the live database before designing against them; confirm migrations actually landed after applying), prove-it (end-of-work evidence protocol — discovers what CI actually gates, runs both static gates, checks threaded values at their terminus, performs one real persistence round-trip, and emits a claim→command→result table where anything unprovable is labeled UNVERIFIED rather than assumed), review-slop (report-only diff review with evidence, calibrated severity, validation and mock-coverage checks, and acceptance criteria), review-merge-pipeline (verify → review → fix → commit → push → PR → merge in one shot, detecting the repo's integration branch instead of assuming one and merging only the commit whose required checks passed), deploy (production promotion with merge strategy inferred from repository history), db-migration-safety (expand-contract sequencing, idempotent SQL, batched backfills), backup-verify (confirms backups exist AND actually restore, via a scratch branch with smoke queries and timestamped evidence), and ship-issues (takes a batch of issues from intake to production in one run: grounds and groups them, reports status before any edit, calls the skills above per group, then validates against production). Every skill defers to a repo-local version of itself when the project defines one.

plugins.name: work-plan
plugins.description: Track-aware daily planning over GitHub issues. Shared tracks (git-synced .work-plan/) optionally pinned to a canonical plan branch (plan-branch; push-track promotes a private track to it), AI clustering (group/auto-triage), coverage, plan-status doc liveness with drift detection, batched GraphQL fetches, and dependency-aware next-up with per-track ordering presets. Includes a theme-aware, accessible VS Code viewer — sidebar tree with a visibility×tier exposure badge, a repo-qualified Mermaid dependency graph, per-issue in-progress badge/toggle and dependency chips, next-up controls, proactive auto-slot suggestions with a compare-and-swap collision guard, and a Plans view with confirm-gated frontmatter writes and repository-contained plan links. Installer ownership is content-verified so unmanaged or modified launchers are preserved.

plugins.name: defect-scan
plugins.description: Language-aware defect hunter for Claude Code AND Codex. Detect stack -> triage by risk -> run real analyzers (ruff/mypy, tsc/eslint, rubocop/brakeman, +optional semgrep/gitleaks/bandit) -> reason with battle-tested patterns + 15 language profiles (python, react-typescript, ruby, go, csharp, java, kotlin, swift, objc, php, rust, yaml, shell, dart) -> report (confidence-tiered, severity/priority, gh-issue-correlated) -> optionally file deduped/labeled issues (--file-issues), apply safe fixes (--fix), or second-opinion via Codex (--cross-model). Runs on macOS/Linux/Windows (WSL/Git-Bash or PowerShell shim); model-free eval harness; extensible drop-in profiles/patterns.

plugins.name: product-strategy
plugins.description: A chief product manager and teacher, thirteen focused skills and a business-capability specialist for deciding what to build and why. Works through vision, strategy, value proposition, objectives and North Star metrics, roadmaps, discovery and experiments, growth, market analysis and team design, labelling evidence and assumptions as it goes and explaining each choice for people without product training.

plugins.name: go-to-market
plugins.description: A head of marketing and eleven focused skills for positioning, audience, copy, brand, search and answer-engine visibility, launches, community, founder-led content, outreach, lifecycle email and measurement. Built for small teams and solo builders: plans start from a goal and the hours you actually have, favour honest persuasion over tricks, and explain the marketing reasoning as they go.
